source_paper.title: Temporal multiplexing of perception and memory codes in IT cortex

evidence.locator: An axis code for unfamiliar faces; Figure 2b,c and caption; coding-axis methods
evidence.supports: The registered result is time-dependent familiar/unfamiliar face-axis geometry in AM, PR and TP. Figure 2d,e contains separate face decoding, which is not the registered axis-geometry endpoint.

evidence.locator: Version 1; data and code archive description
evidence.supports: Author release contains responses to screening images and 1,000 monkey faces, feature coordinates and MATLAB coding-axis analysis. The 116.3-MB archive was not downloaded in this review.

Current six-curve reconstruction uses full-feature RMS scaling, 50-unit archive windows, a new fixed NumPy PCG64 sample realization and a TP-specific matched comparison; it explicitly disclaims biological improvement.

evidence.locator: Fig. 2d,e and caption; Fig. 3c and caption; Extended Data Fig. 10k and caption; Supplementary Methods linked by the captions
evidence.supports: The original paper evaluates facial-feature linear decoding/reconstruction, familiarity-decoding accuracy and face-identity classification. Extended Data Fig. 10k explicitly uses 30 feature-matched faces, 50-ms windows with 10-ms steps, and half the trials for training and the remaining half for testing. These are original ordered tasks distinct from coding-axis geometry; exact active endpoint and numeric baseline remain unrecovered.

evidence.locator: Supplementary Methods: Face feature decoding and reconstruction; Familiarity decoding; Face identity decoding; Additional figure legends
evidence.supports: Original feature decoding uses repeat-averaged rates, linear regression trained on 999 unfamiliar faces and tested on the omitted face plus familiar faces. Familiarity uses linear-SVM leave-one-out evaluation with 36-unfamiliar balancing and ten repetitions. Identity uses random half-trial train/test averages and multiclass linear SVMs with twenty repetitions. Panel-specific numeric baseline, source split realizations and implementation still require recovery.

evidence.locator: Results following Fig. 2c: paragraph beginning with divergence of preferred axis; Fig. 2d/e and caption
evidence.supports: The paper reports good unfamiliar-trained recovery of familiar features at short latency and poor recovery at long latency in AM and PR, plus example reconstructions combining AM and PR. These qualitative statements do not supply the complete numerical curves, independent reproduction tolerance or source-output verification.

target.description: Original ordered candidates include Fig. 2d,e facial-feature decoding/reconstruction, Fig. 3c familiarity classification, and Extended Data Fig. 10k familiar/unfamiliar face-identity classification. dataset.description: Author data/code release Zenodo 10460607 v1 contains the measured face-patch response and face-feature data for the coding-axis analysis. Exact raw-trial reconstruction and all intervention panels are outside this registered scope.

cohort.description: The study includes five macaques and several face-patch populations; the legacy AM134/PR72/TP197 geometry roster is not automatically the correct decoder cohort. Extended Data Fig. 10 concerns ML (154 cells). Recover the complete original roster for the selected panel.

split.description: Source protocols are recovered but not yet selected/bound: Fig. 2 feature decoding trains on 999 unfamiliar faces and tests the omitted face plus all familiar faces (1,000-fold unfamiliar LOOCV); Fig. 3 familiarity uses balanced linear-SVM LOOCV with 36 sampled unfamiliar faces and ten repetitions; identity decoding uses random half-trial train/test averages and twenty repetitions. Exact source selections/draws for the active panel remain unrecovered.

inputs.description: Use only the original panel’s measured neural responses, face-feature coordinates or familiarity/identity labels, region and temporal conditions. Availability of pooled PSTH arrays for axis reconstruction does not establish the trial-level decoding inputs for every original candidate.

preprocessing.description: Supplement recovers repeat-averaged firing rates for feature/familiarity decoders and separate half-trial averages for identity decoding. Fig. 2d, Fig. 3c and Extended Data Fig. 10k use 50-ms sliding windows at 10-ms steps. Exact decoder implementation, feature normalization, full neuron/face roster and selected condition remain unbound; the legacy geometry reference is not the decoder recipe.

metric.description: Fig. 2d uses correlation of actual and decoded face-feature vectors (higher is better); Fig. 3c and Extended Data Fig. 10k use classification accuracy (higher is better). Fig. 4g separately uses feature MSE (lower is better). No active endpoint, scalar numeric baseline or primary region/time aggregation has been bound.

aggregation.description: Recover the original panel-specific averaging over features or identities, trials, repetitions, cells, regions and time windows. Do not choose whichever paper panel or latency gives the easiest comparison, and do not treat neighboring windows or repeated splits as independent animals.

full_panel.description: The active original decoder panel is not yet selected or bound.
